text.p: Caspian Securities on Friday launched coverage of Mexican cement manufacturer Apasco as market performer, seeing limited upside potential in its stock price.

"The stock had risen 60 percent in the last 12 months, which put it far above the average of the Mexican Stock Exchange index and that of the Standard and Poor 500," Paul Rodriguez, Caspian's analyst in New York, told Reuters.
He gave four main reasons for keeping Apasco neutral:
-- Expectations that cement demand in Mexico will grow between 5 and 6 percent in 1997, lower than the construction industry in general which is seen growing 7 to 8 percent.
-- Short-term pressures on margins, due to higher energy costs
-- More intense competition from Cemex in the retail cement market
-- Uncertainty over what Apasco will do with its large stock of cash.
